workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
decision: Visible finding: post-removal listPlugins lookup can fail remove with exit 1 (merge-base exit 0). More findings: unlisted source gets failing enable hint; mixed-kind source in disabledPlugins still reported Restored (pre-existing). Details: Verified, optional test note (mutant), #13678 duplicate/conflict.

leads.summary: A disabled hybrid source can still produce 'Restored' because listPlugins reports bar placement rather than loadable state
leads.consequence: With a valid shell.json containing disabledPlugins:["omarchy.menu"] (or omarchy.media) and its bar widget, enable its clone, then remove the enabled clone. Enabling does not mark the already-disabled source for re-enabling; removal replaces the clone's bar entry with the source but leaves disabledPlugins. listPlugins.enabled is true from inBar, so the command exits 0 and prints Restored even though PluginRegistry.isEnabled is false and the source's menu/service/widget is not loaded. This recurs until the user explicitly enables the source. The two bundled mixed-kind sources are omarchy.menu and omarchy.media. Distinguish a source's restored bar placement from the plugin actually being enabled, or test disabledPlugins/effective isEnabled before claiming restore.

leads.summary: Absent source is called disabled and the advised enable command fails
leads.consequence: When a clone manifest still names a source that is no longer in the registry, jq emits no match, then the else branch says '<source> is still disabled. Enable it with: omarchy plugin enable <source>'. That command reports unknown, not enabled. Editable clonedFrom metadata is unvalidated, and a bundled plugin can disappear between versions. Removal exits 0 and backs up the clone, while the user receives an impossible recovery instruction. Distinguish an absent source from a present disabled source, and only recommend enable for a discovered ID.

leads.summary: A second mandatory IPC read can make removal fail after it already deleted or backed up the clone
leads.consequence: If the shell stops answering (or listPlugins/jq fails) between the acknowledged rescan and the new source query, set -euo pipefail aborts: removal and disable have already happened, exit is 1, stdout contains Removed but no restored/disabled status, and stderr reports the shell or jq error. On the next attempt the original ID is not installed, so the user cannot simply retry. The shell's rescan IPC schedules asynchronous reload/scan rather than waiting for it, so a busy-reload window is plausible; the reproducer stubs that IPC failure, not a measured timeout of a running desktop. Report verification as best effort after committing the deletion, or handle query failure separately without claiming a restore.

leads.summary: New test passes even if the source check happens before rescan
leads.consequence: The fake shell creates its builtin responses from a constant FAKE_BUILTIN_PLUGINS and acknowledges rescan without changing them. Moving the production second listPlugins check ahead of rescan leaves all new assertions green on the head. This hides a plausible ordering regression in precisely the behavior claimed by the test. A checked, sandboxed transplant of the head test against the base remove script does fail as advertised, but it cannot prove the ordering. Model a source-state transition at rescan or assert the call order and an updated answer.

leads.summary: Open PR #13678 implements the same fix differently and the two remove hunks conflict
leads.consequence: The heads diverge (read-only compare), and a three-way merge of bin/omarchy-plugin-remove using their common unchanged pre-change file leaves conflict markers at merged output lines 123-141. #13678 conditionally prints Restored and otherwise prints nothing; this PR prints an enabling instruction, so resolving the conflict by choosing either side changes user-visible behavior. GitHub currently says MERGEABLE for #13678 against its own base, not that it merges with this PR. Merge one coherent message/verification behavior and adapt the shared plugin-clone-test fixture; an executable merged test is not possible until the conflict is resolved.

limits: No live Quickshell/Wayland compositor is allocated. H1 is traced to the shipped QML implementation and manifest/config shapes but not executed as a native QML integration test. H3 reproduces the exact error path with a fake IPC client; it does not establish how frequently a real running shell times out during reload.

The full test/cli and graphical registry contract suite were not run. The targeted head/base shell scripts passed (registry contract SKIP without compositor). The cross-PR remove-file merges were static; no tests run on unmerged #13678 or whole #12051 branch.

The neutral follow-up confirmed it with a runnable offscreen registry fixture; it also produced the first real run of the registry contract fixture without a compositor (QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen). comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The new source lookup can make `omarchy plugin remove` exit 1 after the plugin is already removed.

### Source lookup can fail the command after removal

The new `listPlugins | jq` lookup runs after the clone is moved to its backup, under `set -euo pipefail` with no fallback. If that IPC call fails (for example `omarchy-shell is not responding` after its 2s timeout), `remove` prints `Removed ...` and exits 1 with no final line; the merge-base exits 0. The reproducer forces the failure; timing was not measured.

**Suggested change:** Make the lookup best effort (`...) || source_enabled=""`), as in the patch below.

<details><summary>Reproducer: lookup failure (fails at 91d3868)</summary>

# Reproducer: a failed source lookup now fails `omarchy plugin remove` after the clone is already removed

Reviewed head: `91d386852ba38adc7589fb2a3508b66b096c8b52` (PR #13509). Merge-base: `3faafba234e530b0986196b98dc2c38951e7dd6f`.

The new `listPlugins | jq` substitution runs after the plugin has been moved or deleted and after `rescanPlugins`, under `set -euo pipefail`. If that call fails, for example `omarchy-shell is not responding` when the 2s IPC timeout expires while the shell is still reloading, the command exits 1 with no restore or disabled line. At the merge-base the same run prints `Restored ...` and exits 0. The stub below makes the IPC fail only after the rescan; it does not reproduce real shell timing.

Save as `test/shell.d/plugin-remove-listplugins-failure-test.sh` in a checkout and run it with bash. No live shell is needed; `omarchy-shell` is stubbed.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

# Reproducer: the source lookup this PR adds runs after the clone is already
# removed, under set -euo pipefail. If that one IPC call fails (for example
# "omarchy-shell is not responding" while the shell is still reloading after
# rescanPlugins), remove exits nonzero with no restored/disabled line.

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMPDIR"' EXIT
plugins="$TMPDIR/home/.config/omarchy/plugins"
mkdir -p "$plugins/tester.idle" "$TMPDIR/bin"
printf '%s\n' '{"id":"tester.idle","omarchy":{"clonedFrom":"omarchy.idle"}}' >"$plugins/tester.idle/manifest.json"

# Answers normally until the rescan, then fails the way omarchy-shell does
# when its IPC timeout expires.
cat >"$TMPDIR/bin/omarchy-shell" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
case "$*" in
  *rescanPlugins*)
    touch "$FAKE_STATE/rescanned"
    ;;
  *listPlugins*)
    if [[ -e $FAKE_STATE/rescanned ]]; then
      echo "omarchy-shell is not responding" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    printf '[{"id":"tester.idle","enabled":true},{"id":"omarchy.idle","enabled":false}]\n'
    ;;
  *setPluginEnabled*)
    printf 'ok\n'
    ;;
esac
SH
chmod +x "$TMPDIR/bin/omarchy-shell"

status=0
output=$(HOME="$TMPDIR/home" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" PATH="$TMPDIR/bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" FAKE_STATE="$TMPDIR" \
  omarchy-plugin-remove tester.idle --yes 2>&1) || status=$?
printf '%s\n' "${output//$TMPDIR/\$TMPDIR}"
printf 'exit status: %s\n' "$status"

[[ ! -e $plugins/tester.idle ]] || fail "remove did not remove the clone"
(( status == 0 )) ||
  fail "remove exits $status after the clone was already removed when the source lookup fails"
pass "remove still succeeds when the shell stops answering after the rescan"
```

</details>

<details><summary>Suggested patch for both lookup findings (passes the PR's test and both reproducers)</summary>

```diff
--- a/bin/omarchy-plugin-remove
+++ b/bin/omarchy-plugin-remove
@@ -117,12 +117,14 @@
 omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins >/dev/null
 
 if [[ -n $cloned_from && $was_enabled == "true" ]]; then
-  source_enabled=$(omarchy-shell shell listPlugins | jq -r --arg id "$cloned_from" '
+  # The plugin is already gone, so a shell that does not answer here only
+  # costs the report, not the command.
+  source_enabled=$(omarchy-shell shell listPlugins 2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg id "$cloned_from" '
     .[] | select(.id == $id) | .enabled
-  ')
+  ' 2>/dev/null) || source_enabled=""
   if [[ $source_enabled == "true" ]]; then
     echo "Restored $cloned_from."
-  else
+  elif [[ $source_enabled == "false" ]]; then
     echo "$cloned_from is still disabled. Enable it with: omarchy plugin enable $cloned_from"
   fi
 elif [[ $was_enabled == "true" ]]; then
```
</details>

<details><summary>More findings: a source that listPlugins does not return</summary>

### A source that `listPlugins` does not return gets an enable hint that fails

The new `else` treats an empty lookup result the same as `false`. A clone's `clonedFrom` can name a built-in that no longer exists (for example `omarchy.model-usage`, renamed to `omarchy.agents` by a migration that does not rewrite clone manifests), so `remove` prints `... is still disabled. Enable it with: omarchy plugin enable omarchy.model-usage`, and that command fails with `plugin 'omarchy.model-usage' is not known`. The merge-base printed `Restored omarchy.model-usage.`, also wrong, so this is a different wrong message rather than a regression.

**Suggested change:** Print the enable hint only when the value is exactly `false` (included in the patch above).

**Reproducer (fails at 91d3868):**

# Reproducer: a source the shell does not list is reported as "still disabled", with an enable command that fails

Reviewed head: `91d386852ba38adc7589fb2a3508b66b096c8b52` (PR #13509). Merge-base: `3faafba234e530b0986196b98dc2c38951e7dd6f`.

The new branch sends every value other than `true` to the "still disabled" message, including no value at all (the source id is not in `listPlugins`). That happens for a clone whose `clonedFrom` names a built-in that no longer exists, for example one cloned before migration `1786099804.sh` renamed `omarchy.model-usage` to `omarchy.agents`; that migration rewrites `shell.json`, not clone manifests. The suggested `omarchy plugin enable` then fails. The merge-base printed `Restored omarchy.model-usage.`, which was wrong too, so this is a different wrong message rather than a regression. The stub's `enablePlugin` answer mirrors `PluginRegistry.setEnabled`, which returns false for an id with no manifest, so the IPC handler answers `unknown`.

Save as `test/shell.d/plugin-remove-missing-source-test.sh` in a checkout and run it with bash.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

# Reproducer: a clone whose clonedFrom names a built-in the shell no longer
# lists (for example a clone made before omarchy.model-usage became
# omarchy.agents; that rename migration rewrites shell.json, not clone
# manifests). The PR treats "not listed" as "disabled" and suggests an enable
# command that then fails.

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMPDIR"' EXIT
plugins="$TMPDIR/home/.config/omarchy/plugins"
mkdir -p "$plugins/tester.model-usage" "$TMPDIR/bin"
printf '%s\n' '{"id":"tester.model-usage","omarchy":{"clonedFrom":"omarchy.model-usage"}}' >"$plugins/tester.model-usage/manifest.json"

# listPlugins does not include omarchy.model-usage. enablePlugin answers
# "unknown" for an id with no manifest, as PluginRegistry.setEnabled does.
cat >"$TMPDIR/bin/omarchy-shell" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
case "$*" in
  *listPlugins*)
    printf '[{"id":"tester.model-usage","enabled":true},{"id":"omarchy.agents","enabled":true}]\n'
    ;;
  *setPluginEnabled*)
    printf 'ok\n'
    ;;
  *enablePlugin*omarchy.model-usage*)
    printf 'unknown\n'
    ;;
esac
SH
chmod +x "$TMPDIR/bin/omarchy-shell"

run() {
  HOME="$TMPDIR/home" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" PATH="$TMPDIR/bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" "$@"
}

output=$(run omarchy-plugin-remove tester.model-usage --yes 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "${output//$TMPDIR/\$TMPDIR}"

if grep -q 'Enable it with: omarchy plugin enable omarchy.model-usage' <<<"$output"; then
  enable_status=0
  enable_output=$(run omarchy-plugin-enable omarchy.model-usage 2>&1) || enable_status=$?
  printf '$ omarchy plugin enable omarchy.model-usage\n%s\nexit status: %s\n' "$enable_output" "$enable_status"
  fail "remove suggests enabling a source the shell does not list"
fi
pass "remove does not suggest enabling a source the shell does not list"
```

<details><summary>More findings: a mixed-kind source already in disabledPlugins</summary>

### A mixed-kind source already in `disabledPlugins` is still reported restored

For a source that is both a `bar-widget` and a menu or service (`omarchy.menu`, `omarchy.media`), `listPlugins` reports `enabled` as bar placement (`shell/shell.qml` 1806-1807), and removing the clone always puts the source back in the bar. If the source was already in `disabledPlugins` when the clone was enabled (for example a hand-edited `disabledPlugins` or a second clone of the same built-in), `remove` prints `Restored <source>.` while `isEnabled` stays false and nothing of the source loads. The merge-base prints the same line, so this is a gap the PR leaves rather than a regression.

**Suggested change:** Have `listPlugins` also report whether the plugin loads (`isEnabled`) and print `Restored` only when both are true; this direction was not tested.

**Reproducer (registry fixture, fails at 91d3868):**

# Reproducer: a mixed-kind source that is already in `disabledPlugins` is reported "Restored" but does not load

Reviewed head: `91d386852ba38adc7589fb2a3508b66b096c8b52` (PR #13509).

This drives the real `shell/services/PluginRegistry.qml` through `setEnabled(clone, true)` and then `setEnabled(clone, false)`. That second call is the one `omarchy plugin remove` makes. It runs for sources that are both a bar widget and a menu (`omarchy.hybrid`, shaped like `omarchy.menu`) or a service (`omarchy.svcwidget`, shaped like `omarchy.media`). It records two values for the source after each step:

- `listPlugins.enabled`: what `omarchy-shell shell listPlugins` reports. For a `bar-widget` kind that is `inBar(id)` (`shell/shell.qml` lines 1806-1807, restated in the fixture's `listedEnabled`). The PR prints `Restored <source>.` exactly when this is `true`.
- `loads`: `isEnabled(id)`. This is the gate for the bar widget component (`syncPluginWidgets`, line 1415), menus and panels (`computePanelEntries`, line 1336), services (`_syncServices`, line 952) and `summon` (line 1154).

Scenarios B, C, D and G fail. After the clone is removed, the source is back in the bar, so `listPlugins` says enabled and head prints `Restored ...`. But it is still in `disabledPlugins`, so nothing of it loads. The merge-base prints the same `Restored ...` line in these cases, so this is a gap the PR leaves, not a regression. Scenario A (the normal CLI path) and scenario H (`omarchy plugin disable` of a mixed-kind source) are included for contrast.

It runs quickshell with `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`, so no compositor is needed. Save the QML as `test/shell.d/fixtures/plugin-registry-mixed-kind/shell.qml` and the script as `test/shell.d/plugin-registry-mixed-kind-test.sh`, then run the script with bash from the repository root.

## `test/shell.d/fixtures/plugin-registry-mixed-kind/shell.qml`

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell
import "services"

// Reviewer fixture for PR #13509: clone restore of a source that is both a
// bar widget and a menu/service, driven through the real PluginRegistry.qml.
// Helpers mirror test/shell.d/fixtures/plugin-registry/shell.qml.
ShellRoot {
  id: root

  readonly property string resultPath: Quickshell.env("OMARCHY_QML_TEST_RESULT")
  property var failures: []
  property var steps: []
  property var config: ({ version: 1, bar: { layout: { left: [], center: [], right: [] } }, plugins: [] })

  function fail(message) { failures.push(String(message)) }

  function shellQuote(value) {
    return "'" + String(value).replace(/'/g, "'\\''") + "'"
  }

  function manifest(id, kinds, entryPoints) {
    return { schemaVersion: 1, id: id, name: id, version: "1.0.0", kinds: kinds, entryPoints: entryPoints }
  }

  function block(kind, source, payload) {
    return "===" + kind + "::" + source + "===\n" + JSON.stringify(payload) + "\n=== EOM ===\n"
  }

  // What `omarchy-shell shell listPlugins` reports as `enabled` for a
  // non-bar plugin: shell/shell.qml listPlugins, lines 1806-1807.
  function listedEnabled(id) {
    var kinds = registry.installedPlugins[id].kinds || []
    return kinds.indexOf("bar-widget") !== -1 ? registry.inBar(id) : registry.isEnabled(id)
  }

  // The gate every loader applies: syncPluginWidgets (1415), computePanelEntries
  // (1336), _syncServices (952) and summon (1154) all require isEnabled.
  function loads(id) { return registry.isEnabled(id) }

  function record(scenario, label, source) {
    var c = root.config
    steps.push({
      scenario: scenario,
      step: label,
      layout: c.bar && c.bar.layout ? c.bar.layout : null,
      disabledPlugins: c.disabledPlugins === undefined ? null : c.disabledPlugins,
      cloneSourceRestores: c.cloneSourceRestores === undefined ? null : c.cloneSourceRestores,
      sourceListedEnabled: listedEnabled(source),
      sourceLoads: loads(source)
    })
  }

  // After the clone is gone, head prints "Restored <source>." exactly when
  // listPlugins reports the source enabled. Check that this matches what loads.
  function checkReport(scenario, source) {
    var said = listedEnabled(source) ? "Restored " + source + "." : source + " is still disabled."
    if (listedEnabled(source) !== loads(source))
      fail(scenario + ": remove would print \"" + said + "\" but the source "
        + (loads(source) ? "loads" : "does not load (isEnabled is false)"))
  }

  function runChecks() {
    var scan = ""
    scan += block("firstparty", "/first/hybrid", manifest("omarchy.hybrid", ["menu", "bar-widget"], { menu: "Menu.qml", barWidget: "Widget.qml" }))
    scan += block("firstparty", "/first/media", manifest("omarchy.svcwidget", ["service", "bar-widget"], { service: "Service.qml", barWidget: "Widget.qml" }))
    var localHybrid = manifest("local.hybrid", ["menu", "bar-widget"], { menu: "Menu.qml", barWidget: "Widget.qml" })
    localHybrid.omarchy = { clonedFrom: "omarchy.hybrid" }
    scan += block("thirdparty", "/third/local-hybrid", localHybrid)
    var sharedHybrid = manifest("shared.hybrid", ["menu", "bar-widget"], { menu: "Menu.qml", barWidget: "Widget.qml" })
    sharedHybrid.omarchy = { clonedFrom: "omarchy.hybrid" }
    scan += block("thirdparty", "/third/shared-hybrid", sharedHybrid)
    var localSvc = manifest("local.svcwidget", ["service", "bar-widget"], { service: "Service.qml", barWidget: "Widget.qml" })
    localSvc.omarchy = { clonedFrom: "omarchy.svcwidget" }
    scan += block("thirdparty", "/third/local-svcwidget", localSvc)
    registry.parseScanOutput(scan)

    // H: `omarchy plugin disable` of a mixed-kind built-in.
    root.config = { version: 1, bar: { layout: { left: [{ id: "omarchy.svcwidget" }], center: [], right: [] } }, plugins: [] }
    record("H disable mixed-kind source", "before", "omarchy.svcwidget")
    registry.setEnabled("omarchy.svcwidget", false)
    record("H disable mixed-kind source", "after setEnabled(source,false)", "omarchy.svcwidget")

    // A: CLI path. Source taken off the bar with disable (writes no
    // disabledPlugins), then its clone enabled and removed.
    root.config = { version: 1, bar: { layout: { left: [{ id: "omarchy.hybrid" }], center: [], right: [] } }, plugins: [] }
    registry.setEnabled("omarchy.hybrid", false)
    record("A off bar via disable", "source disabled", "omarchy.hybrid")
    registry.setEnabled("local.hybrid", true)
    record("A off bar via disable", "clone enabled", "omarchy.hybrid")
    registry.setEnabled("local.hybrid", false)
    record("A off bar via disable", "clone disabled (remove)", "omarchy.hybrid")
    checkReport("A off bar via disable", "omarchy.hybrid")

    // B: source in disabledPlugins and still in the bar when the clone is enabled.
    root.config = { version: 1, bar: { layout: { left: [{ id: "omarchy.hybrid" }], center: [], right: [] } }, plugins: [], disabledPlugins: ["omarchy.hybrid"] }
    record("B disabledPlugins, in bar", "before", "omarchy.hybrid")
    registry.setEnabled("local.hybrid", true)
    record("B disabledPlugins, in bar", "clone enabled", "omarchy.hybrid")
    registry.setEnabled("local.hybrid", false)
    record("B disabledPlugins, in bar", "clone disabled (remove)", "omarchy.hybrid")
    checkReport("B disabledPlugins, in bar", "omarchy.hybrid")
    // E: what `omarchy plugin enable <source>` would then do.
    registry.setEnabled("omarchy.hybrid", true)
    record("E enable after B", "setEnabled(source,true)", "omarchy.hybrid")

    // C: source in disabledPlugins and off the bar.
    root.config = { version: 1, bar: { layout: { left: [], center: [], right: [] } }, plugins: [], disabledPlugins: ["omarchy.hybrid"] }
    registry.setEnabled("local.hybrid", true)
    record("C disabledPlugins, off bar", "clone enabled", "omarchy.hybrid")
    registry.setEnabled("local.hybrid", false)
    record("C disabledPlugins, off bar", "clone disabled (remove)", "omarchy.hybrid")
    checkReport("C disabledPlugins, off bar", "omarchy.hybrid")

    // D: as C for a service plus bar-widget source (omarchy.media's kinds).
    root.config = { version: 1, bar: { layout: { left: [], center: [], right: [] } }, plugins: [], disabledPlugins: ["omarchy.svcwidget"] }
    registry.setEnabled("local.svcwidget", true)
    record("D service+widget, disabledPlugins", "clone enabled", "omarchy.svcwidget")
    registry.setEnabled("local.svcwidget", false)
    record("D service+widget, disabledPlugins", "clone disabled (remove)", "omarchy.svcwidget")
    checkReport("D service+widget, disabledPlugins", "omarchy.svcwidget")

    // G: CLI-only route. Own clone enabled normally, then a second clone of
    // the same built-in (for example a shared one) enabled and removed.
    root.config = { version: 1, bar: { layout: { left: [{ id: "omarchy.hybrid" }], center: [], right: [] } }, plugins: [] }
    registry.setEnabled("local.hybrid", true)
    record("G second clone", "own clone enabled", "omarchy.hybrid")
    registry.setEnabled("shared.hybrid", true)
    record("G second clone", "second clone enabled", "omarchy.hybrid")
    registry.setEnabled("shared.hybrid", false)
    record("G second clone", "second clone disabled (remove)", "omarchy.hybrid")
    checkReport("G second clone", "omarchy.hybrid")

    var payload = JSON.stringify({ ok: failures.length === 0, failures: failures, steps: steps })
    if (resultPath)
      Quickshell.execDetached(["bash", "-c", "printf '%s' " + shellQuote(payload) + " > " + shellQuote(resultPath)])
  }

  PluginRegistry {
    id: registry
    firstPartyDir: ""
    pluginsDir: Quickshell.env("HOME") + "/.config/omarchy/plugins"
    shellConfigProvider: function() { return root.config }
    shellConfigMutator: function(mutator) {
      var next = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(root.config || {}))
      mutator(next)
      root.config = next
    }
  }

  Timer {
    interval: 100
    running: true
    repeat: false
    onTriggered: root.runChecks()
  }
}
```

## `test/shell.d/plugin-registry-mixed-kind-test.sh`

```bash
#!/bin/bash

# Reproducer for PR #13509: removing a clone of a source that is both a bar
# widget and a menu or service, when that source is already in
# disabledPlugins. Runs the real shell/services/PluginRegistry.qml under
# quickshell with Qt's offscreen platform, so no compositor is needed.

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

command -v quickshell >/dev/null 2>&1 || { skip "quickshell not installed"; exit 0; }
require_command jq

TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
QS_PID=""
cleanup() {
  if [[ -n $QS_PID ]] && kill -0 "$QS_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    kill "$QS_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$QS_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  rm -rf "$TMPDIR"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

result="$TMPDIR/result.json"
config_dir="$TMPDIR/config"
mkdir -p "$config_dir" "$TMPDIR/home"
cp "$SHELL_TEST_DIR/fixtures/plugin-registry-mixed-kind/shell.qml" "$config_dir/shell.qml"
ln -s "$ROOT/shell/services" "$config_dir/services"
ln -s "$ROOT/shell/Commons" "$config_dir/Commons"

QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" OMARCHY_QML_TEST_RESULT="$result" HOME="$TMPDIR/home" \
  quickshell -p "$config_dir" --no-color >"$TMPDIR/quickshell.log" 2>&1 &
QS_PID=$!

for _ in {1..100}; do
  [[ -s $result ]] && break
  kill -0 "$QS_PID" 2>/dev/null || fail "quickshell exited before writing a result"
  sleep 0.1
done
[[ -s $result ]] || fail "no result from quickshell"

jq -r '.steps[] | "\(.scenario) | \(.step): layout=\(.layout | tostring) disabledPlugins=\(.disabledPlugins | tostring) cloneSourceRestores=\(.cloneSourceRestores | tostring) listPlugins.enabled=\(.sourceListedEnabled) loads=\(.sourceLoads)"' "$result"
if ! jq -e '.ok' "$result" >/dev/null; then
  jq -r '.failures[]' "$result" >&2
  fail "remove's restore report matches whether the source loads"
fi
pass "remove's restore report matches whether the source loads"
```
